title: Try a frame on each kind of text
statement: A question frame designed on one kind of text must be tried on each other kind before it is used there.
detail: A closing-question frame whose slots ask "when", written and worked through on a story, was used in an informational lesson, and its model answers came out as a part doing its job when it does its job, because that text has no event to point at. A review of a story lesson found the same slot worked there because the text was a story.
against: The spec and the checker treat the pattern as text-neutral: "Nothing in the pattern is fiction-specific." (`shadow-content-eval/references/closing_questions_pattern.md`, lines 8-9). The finding rests on one informational lesson, and the review left the fix open: "Nonfiction probably needs its own frame variant" (`shadow-content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-review.md`, line 83).

evidence.quote: That says "a part does its job when it does its job".
- The spec's "when, not what" rule is written for narrative, where "when" gets the mechanism. Here there is no event to point at.
"When" works here because the text is a story.
